habitat: Usually in pairs or groups in broad-leaved woodland and thornveld, feeding mainly on the ground.
summary: A fairly common resident. A medium-sized woodpecker with spotted underparts, except in Namibia, where it is unspotted. The male has an entirely red crown and a red malar streak. The female has brown patches on the face and throat, and Newman’s identification line gives her a red nape. The call is an excitable high-pitched chattering, sometimes by two or three birds together and often with wing-flapping. Bill colour, eye, legs, wings and the tail colour were not described. The Kemp paper name Bennett’s Woodpecker and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Golden-tailed Woodpecker is streaked below rather than spotted. Its female has a spotted black-and-white crown, not brown patches on the face and throat.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common resident, and Avibase does not mark the Kruger occurrence rare or accidental, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The female red nape is on Newman’s identification line. The description itself names the brown face and throat. The immature was not described. Bill colour, eye, legs, wings and tail colour were not given. No female photograph and no flight photograph were found. The Kruger frames are two males, a side at Malalane Gate and a front at Malelane Camp, both CC0. The grade A recording is a duet from North Luangwa. A grade A drumming from Nylsvley was not used, because Newman does not describe drumming for this species. Population figures, the Kemp paper name Bennett’s Woodpecker and the code RB were left unchanged.
